states.claim: rtcp_xr is a typed pointer to the same storage region as the byte-addressed input pkt.
rb_hdr points to the buf subobject/interior region of the rtcp_xr packet storage.
rb_rr_time is set to point to the current rb_hdr report block when its block type is BT_RR_TIME.
states.evidence:
L30: case BT_RR_TIME:
L31: rb_rr_time = (pjmedia_rtcp_xr_rb_rr_time*) rb_hdr;

states.evidence:

L34: rb_dlrr = (pjmedia_rtcp_xr_rb_dlrr*) rb_hdr;

states.evidence:

states.claim: rb_hdr is advanced to the next report block within the packet storage region.
rb_rr_time remains NULL unless a BT_RR_TIME report block was encountered.
rb_dlrr remains NULL unless a BT_DLRR report block was encountered.
rb_stats remains NULL unless a BT_STATS report block was encountered.
rb_voip_mtc remains NULL unless a BT_VOIP_METRICS report block was encountered.

values.claim: pkt_len is the 16-bit network-order RTCP length field; the packet is accepted only when (pkt_len + 1) <= size / 4, so the valid packet extent in 32-bit words is pkt_len + 1 and in bytes is 4*(pkt_len + 1).

rb_hdr starts at rtcp_xr->buf and is advanced by (rb_len + 1) 32-bit words per report block; the loop condition compares the rb_hdr 32-bit pointer against pkt + pkt_len, so the report-block walk is bounded by pkt_len 32-bit words from pkt.

rb_rr_time, rb_dlrr, rb_stats, and rb_voip_mtc are set to the current rb_hdr address when the corresponding block type is encountered, so each points into the packet at a report-block boundary reached by the rb_hdr walk.
eedelay is computed as now - lrr - dlrr in 64-bit unsigned arithmetic, where now, lrr, and dlrr are 32-bit values in 1/65536-second units.
values.evidence:
L80: now = ((ntp.hi & 0xFFFF) << 16) + (ntp.lo >> 16);
L83: eedelay = now - lrr - dlrr;

values.claim: eedelay is converted from 1/65536-second units to microseconds: if eedelay < 4294, eedelay = (eedelay * 1000000) >> 16; otherwise eedelay = ((eedelay * 1000) >> 16) * 1000.
rtt is the low 32 bits of the 64-bit eedelay value, and is only used when eedelay <= 30,000,000 microseconds.
When rtt exceeds three times the existing mean and the sample count is nonzero, rtt is replaced by (unsigned)sess->stat.rtt.mean * 3.
signal_lvl is converted from an unsigned byte to a signed 8-bit value by subtracting 256 when the byte value exceeds 127, then cast to pj_int8_t.
values.evidence:
L194: sess->stat.tx.voip_mtc.signal_lvl = (pj_int8_t)
L195: ((rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl > 127)?
L196: ((int)rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl - 256) :
L197: rb_voip_mtc->signal_lvl);

values.claim: noise_lvl is converted from an unsigned byte to a signed 8-bit value by subtracting 256 when the byte value exceeds 127, then cast to pj_int8_t.
values.evidence:
L198: sess->stat.tx.voip_mtc.noise_lvl  = (pj_int8_t)
L199: ((rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl > 127)?
L200: ((int)rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl - 256) :
L201: rb_voip_mtc->noise_lvl);
